Oxygen consumption data reveals that uphill running approaches ventilatory threshold, constraining performance. These form a closed-loop system where terrain-induced changes in gradient trigger immediate adjustments in stride length, modulated by physiological limits. The predictive model uses a weighted gradient factor to anticipate speed changes, suggesting a memory-based pacing strategy. This implies that GSE can simulate pacing decisions by integrating real-time gradient data with historical speed profiles. The failure mode occurs when physiological limits are exceeded, leading to disproportionate stride shortening or increased fatigue. The mathematical structure reflects a hybrid control system combining mechanical feedback and physiological thresholds.
